newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania forex reserves seen up at $4 bln by end-97.
newsitem.headline: Romania forex reserves seen up at $4 bln by end-97.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) said on Wednesday it expected its foreign exchange reserves to climb to $3 billion in late September or early October from $2 billion at present.
The BNR's reserves are forecast to soar further to $4 billion at end-1997, bank spokesman Adrian Vasilescu told a news conference.
"Adding to our current reserves of $2 billion are also $1.3 billion worth of gold," Vasilescu told reporters alongside Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea.

Increasing Romania's foreign exchange reserves is one of the prime objectives of the centrist government's tough reform programme, launched earlier this year with the support of international lenders.

An International Monetary Fund monitoring mission was due in Bucharest on Wednesday to conduct a routine review of progress in reforms to enable the release of further tranches of a $430 million standby credit approved in April.
Vasilescu said the upward trend was due to external credits and capital inflows from direct and portfolio investors.
Foreign investors have taken on an increasingly active role on Romania's capital markets since the introduction of legislation on portfolio deals.
